## Session note - 2022-10-02
- Priya described a senior schoolmate in the Design department, two years ahead of her, who stayed in the studio until 1 a.m. helping her re-print a ruined thesis binding. She said she has replayed that night many times.
- She also said she struggles badly with insomnia and lies awake replaying conversations. The nights get worse when a call with her parents is coming up, because she gets anxious for days beforehand.
- She said the feeling "started sometime around orientation week this September, when he called my name across the studio and I forgot how to answer."
- She does not want anyone in her cohort to know.

## Session note - 2023-01-18
- More about the person she keeps calling "my senior schoolmate." She rehearsed saying something honest to him before the winter showcase, then said nothing and left early instead.
- In the same conversation she talked about a relationship during her graduate coursework that existed almost entirely online. About three months in early 2023, with Liang Hao, someone she met on a design forum. Almost nobody in her life knows it happened.
- She keeps a note on her phone of things she wants to tell the senior schoolmate someday.
- She told one person about Liang Hao and regretted it immediately. She says she goes quiet and stiff whenever the senior schoolmate is near, and then worries he reads it as dislike.

## Session note - 2023-04-27
- The online relationship ended awkwardly when Liang Hao simply stopped replying. She is still embarrassed about how much she leaned on him, described feeling rejected and "easy to put down," and admitted she still checks whether he ever came back online.
- She said she wanted to keep talking about it here because no one else has heard the whole thing.
- She also went back to the senior schoolmate: she wishes they could be closer than "two people who nod in corridors."

## Session note - 2023-09-14
- Her parents push hard about her career. There have been real fights over her wanting to leave a stable job.
- She saw him at a studio review and could not finish her sentence.
- Their disappointment makes her second-guess herself, and it feeds older insecurities about her appearance and whether she is "good enough."

## Session note - 2024-01-11
- Tension at home: her father did not speak to her for weeks after she decided to stay in the city instead of returning for the family business, and her mother now relays messages between them.
- She referred to "the person I have liked since 2022," then corrected herself: it may really have begun on the department field trip that summer, when he gave her his jacket on the bus at dawn.
- She said arguments at home leave her feeling like a problem to be managed rather than a person.

## Session note - 2024-09-20
- Long stretches of loneliness after moving cities: eating dinner standing at the counter, whole weekends without a conversation, keeping the radio on for company.
- After Wei moved to Shanghai she tried to move on, but she kept comparing everyone she met to him and nothing measured up.
- She said she uses these chats partly so that someone knows what her week was like. They reconnected briefly at an alumni reunion and the old feelings came right back.
- Her insecurities came up again: her accent in presentations, being the quietest person in every room, a long-standing belief that people choose her last.

## Session note - 2025-02-14
- She named him for the first time: Wei. She confirmed he is the senior schoolmate she has been describing all along.
- She rehearses ordinary conversations for days before having them, and she almost sent Wei a message today and deleted it after typing it four times.
- She is still embarrassed about Liang Hao and said she is afraid that saying any of this out loud would cost her the small amount of Wei she already has.

## Session note - 2025-11-29
- About Wei: they ended up on the same late train after a workshop and talked for forty minutes about a building they both love. She called it the happiest hour of her year.
- The same night she returned to the fights at home and to whether she is "good enough," then said she wanted to tell Wei then. "I had the whole sentence ready and I gave him a comment about the weather."

- She described Wei as "the person I have liked for four years," counting from her final undergraduate year.

arguments.content:
Wei,

I love you. I have loved you for these past four years, and I have not known how to start.

I think it began on the department field trip, at dawn on the bus, when you gave me your jacket. For a long time I dated it from orientation week that September, the morning you called my name across the studio and I forgot how to answer. I have gone back over both memories, and the jacket was first.

You stayed until one in the morning helping me reprint a thesis binding the printer had ruined. I have replayed that night many times. Before the winter showcase I rehearsed something honest and then left early without saying it. At a studio review I saw you and could not finish my sentence. I go quiet and stiff when you are near, and then I worry you read that as dislike. I wish we were closer than two people who nod in corridors.

When you moved to Shanghai I tried to move on, and I kept comparing everyone I met to you. At the alumni reunion the old feeling came straight back. I keep a note on my phone of things I want to tell you. I almost sent you a message and deleted it after typing it four times. I look for your name first on every project list. I learned to like winter mornings because of one walk.

After the workshop we ended up on the same late train and talked for forty minutes about a building we both love. That was the happiest hour of my year. I had the whole sentence ready, and I gave you a comment about the weather.

I am not asking you to feel the same. I only want you to know.

Priya

There are other things from these years that I have never put next to your name, and I am putting them here too. During my graduate coursework I had a short-lived relationship that existed almost entirely online, with Liang Hao, someone I met on a design forum. It lasted about three months in early 2023. Almost nobody in my life knows it happened. I told one person and regretted it immediately. It ended when he simply stopped replying. I felt rejected and easy to put down, and I still check whether he ever came back online. I am afraid that saying any of this out loud would cost me the small amount of you I already have.

My parents push hard about my career. There have been real fights over my wanting to leave a stable job. My father did not speak to me for weeks after I decided to stay in the city instead of returning for the family business, and my mother now relays messages between us. Those arguments leave me feeling like a problem to be managed rather than a person. The nights are worse when a call with them is coming, because I get anxious for days beforehand and lie awake with insomnia, replaying conversations.

After I moved cities there were long stretches of loneliness: eating dinner standing at the counter, whole weekends without a conversation, keeping the radio on for company. I have insecurities about my appearance and whether I am good enough, about my accent in presentations, about being the quietest person in every room, and a long-standing belief that people choose me last.

I'm Wei Zhang. I'm two years ahead of you in the Design department, so the studio office has put me down as your senior schoolmate for the mentoring list this term.

I still have the old plate-binding jig from my thesis year if your printer keeps chewing the covers. Sunday afternoon in Studio 3 works for me if you want to run the binding again before submission.

Wei

emails.subject: Re: Senior-junior pairing, Design department studio term
emails.body:

Priya

emails.subject: Re: Senior-junior pairing, Design department studio term
emails.body:
Priya,

The department trip list is up - juniors travel on the second bus, seniors on the first, but nobody checks. Bring something warmer than that jacket; the coastal site is cold at six in the morning.

Your section drawings were the clearest on the review wall, for what my opinion is worth as your senior.

Wei
